rationale: C03 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both memoranda describe a bill that overrides a statute of limitations and confers jurisdiction to hear, determine, and render judgment on stale claims; both then defend limitations periods because old evidence becomes unavailable, characterize the proposed waiver as unjustified, and warn that approval would create pressure for equivalent waivers in analogous cases. This combination of distinctive language, legal machinery, and argumentative sequence is materially stronger than the general limitations-policy parallels in C13 and C10.

shared_material.child_excerpt: notwithstanding any statute of limitations or lapse of time, jurisdiction is conferred upon the Court of Claims to hear, determine, and render judgment upon the claims
shared_material.parent_excerpt: jurisdiction would be vested, notwithstanding any statute of limitations or lapse of time, in the United States District Court for the District of New Mexico, "to hear, determine, and render judgment upon any claim against the United States"
shared_material.explanation: Nearly identical jurisdiction-conferring machinery and phrasing, adapted to a different court and class of claims.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The claims were not asserted in timely fashion by the claimants and it is no longer feasible or even possible to obtain the records essential to an adequate presentation of the facts to the Court. This is the very kind of situation which proves the wisdom of a statute of limitation.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The very purpose of a statute of limitations...is to avoid stale claims and to procure a reasonably prompt initiation of judicial action before records are lost or scattered, memories grow dim, and witnesses die or become unavailable...the nature of the claims here involved emphasizes the justice and wisdom of the general rule.
shared_material.explanation: Both apply the same evidentiary-loss rationale to old claims and expressly invoke the wisdom of the limitations rule.

shared_material.child_excerpt: If I were to approve this bill, I could not in all fairness refuse to approve other bills setting aside the statute of limitations on old claims for overtime or other compensation
shared_material.parent_excerpt: an exception as broad as that which S. 417 proposes...would be a precedent for attempts to secure similarly over-generous legislation in the case of every other Federal river-control structure
shared_material.explanation: The child reuses C03's concluding precedent argument, substituting other federal compensation claims for other river-control claims.
